title: You Can Never Become Pope
beats: You want to be pope; the official requirements (Catholic, man) look absurdly thin
Not like becoming president; cardinals pick, and in practice pick one of their own: an unofficial official requirement
Frames the path as a corporate ladder; Step 1 priest, contrasted with online ordination
Priest checklist: degrees, man, unmarried, celibate
Step 2 bishop: 400,000 priests vs 5,000 bishops; cathedrals vs churches; wait for retirement at 75 or death
Nuncio picks three, congress can reset, pope can veto: the pipeline loops back on failure
Run-on chain of 'and you were... and he picked you...' recaps every gate, then 'poof'
Step 3 cardinal: not bosses of bishops, they ARE bishops with an extra title
Only the pope appoints; 200 of 5,000; wait for death or retirement
Conclave: sequestering, four votes a day, 2/3 majority, slow Latin ritual
Ballots burned; TV cameras watch a chimney; black vs white smoke
Typically two weeks, record three years; pick a name by tradition
Funnel recap: half the population, 1 billion, 400,000, 5,000, 200, then 2/3 of cardinals

metrics.misconception: yes: you can run for pope like president (0:17); cardinals outrank bishops (2:47)
metrics.examples: 1 running path; numeric funnel shrinks 1B to 400k to 5k to 200 to 1
metrics.ending: Numeric funnel recap tying back to the thin opening requirements

new_moves.name: new:numeric-funnel
new_moves.what: Attach a population count to each stage so the ladder becomes a shrinking ratio the viewer can feel

new_moves.name: new:run-on-gate-recap
new_moves.what: Restate every conditional gate in one breathless sentence to dramatize compounded improbability

new_moves.what: Distinguish formal rule from de facto rule to reframe the whole problem

theory: The video is a single second-person journey through a pipeline, where each stage has the same three-part template (requirements, scarcity count, who selects). Repetition of the template plus a shrinking number at each stage lets the learner build intuition for 'never' without any argument being stated; the title's claim is proven by the funnel recap.
velocity: Scene builder: offer a 'funnel/pipeline' scene primitive whose stage widths shrink with counts the voice reads aloud
Orchestrator: when teaching a process, use a fixed per-stage template so later stages cost only new content
Voice: at the end of a multi-gate chain, generate one run-on conditional recap to make compound probability felt
Learner model: cast the learner as the protagonist ('you want to...') for procedural topics
Evals: check that every stage of a process lesson states requirement, count, and selector
